clinician.final_diagnosis: Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia (GTN) with WHO score 14
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old woman with sudden onset abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and acute abdomen presented with elevated beta-hCG of 12,712 mUI/mL and free fluid in abdomen without intrauterine pregnancy, suggestive of ectopic or GTN. CT angiogram showed active bleeding from a left renal artery pseudoaneurysm treated by embolization with good clinical response. Beta-hCG initially decreased to 6,230 mUI/mL but later rose sharply to 100,811 mUI/mL with neurological symptoms; brain imaging revealed cerebellar infarct and occipital lesions, and chest CT showed lesions suggesting metastases. Subsequent emergent embolization addressed a right perinephric hematoma. Endometrial biopsy showed inactive endometrium. These findings and clinical course are consistent with high-risk metastatic GTN, staged with WHO score 14.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial beta-hCG of 12,712 mUI/mL at presentation with acute abdomen and free abdominal fluid without intrauterine pregnancy
CT angiogram showed active bleeding from left renal artery pseudoaneurysm on admission
Endovascular embolization performed with good clinical response
Beta-hCG decreased to 6,230 mUI/mL several weeks after initial discharge
Endometrial biopsy showed inactive endometrium, not confirming intrauterine malignancy
Readmission weeks later with neurological symptoms and brain imaging showing right cerebellar infarct and left occipital lesions; beta-hCG rose to 100,811 mUI/mL
During readmission, developed right perinephric hematoma managed by emergent embolization; chest CT revealed lesions suggestive of metastases

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: No intrauterine pregnancy found; high and rising beta-hCG levels plus metastatic lesions inconsistent with isolated ectopic pregnancy
Persistently elevated and rising beta-hCG with metastatic brain and chest lesions and renal artery pseudoaneurysm bleeding supports malignant GTN over benign conditions

remaining_uncertainties: Lack of documented clinical notes explicitly stating WHO scoring and treatment details
No histopathological confirmation of GTN lesions due to inactive endometrial biopsy
No imaging or pathology providing direct tissue confirmation of metastatic GTN
